focus: Advisor prompt hook across runtimes: adapter, single-source import vs copy, timeout and slow/fail emission for Claude, Codex, Cursor, Devin, OpenCode, Pi and dsh.
answeredQuestions: Advisor prompt hook (v4.0.0.1, v4.0.0.2, v4.0.2.0): does every runtime adapter (.claude/hooks, .codex/hooks, .cursor/hooks, .devin/hooks, .opencode/plugins, .pi/extensions, .dsh/plugins) deliver the advisor brief from the single source in .skilled/hooks/skill-advisor, within its time limit?

graphEvents.label: Does every runtime deliver the advisor brief from one source within its time limit?
The advisor matrix omits dsh and names per-runtime advisor targets that cannot exist

label: The maintained advisor matrix is stale in two directions: its header and per-runtime table omit dsh although v4.0.2.0 added and registered the adapter, and it names dist/hooks/codex|devin|cursor/user-prompt-submit.js targets that the advisor package cannot build (only hooks/claude/user-prompt-submit.ts exists, and dist/hooks holds only the claude build). The Codex, Cursor and Devin shims actually spawn the Claude spec-kit adapter (codex/shared.ts:98), which spawns the single Claude advisor handler.

The documented OpenCode timeout control SPECKIT_OPENCODE_HOOK_TIMEOUT_MS (default 3000) is never read by .opencode/plugins/system-skill-advisor.js; the plugin reads SYSTEM_SKILL_ADVISOR_BRIDGE_TIMEOUT_MS and defaults to 2500 ms (line 49, lookup line 376, applied line 392). A timeout resolves as fail_open/TIMEOUT with no brief (line 1285), contradicting the reference's claim that the bridge serves prompt-safe stale context with a timeout marker.

Codex can still lose the fallback the v4.0.0.2 release promised: the codex shim spawns the Claude adapter with a 2800 ms timeout (codex/user-prompt-submit.ts:22) under a 3000 ms host deadline (.codex/hooks.json:49), while the inner adapter reserves 300 ms of startup and fallback margin, so the worst-case chain is 3100 ms. On wrapper timeout runClaudeHookAdapter returns null and no additionalContext is emitted, so the turn gets neither a brief nor the fallback directive. Same wrapper is safe on Cursor and Devin because their hosts allow 10 s.

The dsh advisor adapter awaits core.runAdvisor with no deadline race or timer (prompt-advisor.mjs:168), unlike Pi which races the same in-process call at budget plus 300 ms and renders the fallback on timeout (pi/prompt-advisor.ts:291). The shared handler bounds its CLI spawn at 2500 ms, so the reachable window is narrow, but a stall outside that spawn blocks dsh's serial agent/pre-step waterfall instead of degrading to a fallback. The dsh test covers a throwing core, not a hanging one.

Single source holds for six of seven runtimes: .skilled/hooks/skill-advisor/* is symlinks only, and the one compiled body is system-skill-advisor/runtime/dist/hooks/claude/user-prompt-submit.js. Claude, Codex, Cursor and Devin spawn it through spec-kit shims; Pi and dsh import it in-process; OpenCode is the only separate implementation.

The advisor package dist currently contains only dist/hooks/claude/user-prompt-submit.js and dist/ is gitignored (.gitignore:60), so a checkout that builds only system-spec-kit runs the native hooks with no advisor body. The reference's instruction to build both packages is load-bearing. This is build state, not a tracked defect.

The shared hook's tests were not run: .skilled/hooks/vitest.config.ts exists but the advisor suites live under .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/{runtime/tests,hooks/tests}, and the iteration containment bans repo test/build execution. Test files and case titles were inspected instead.

direction: Four separate compiled advisor handlers, one per native runtime under system-skill-advisor/runtime/dist/hooks/<runtime>
reason: Only the claude handler exists; the Codex, Cursor and Devin shims spawn the Claude spec-kit adapter (codex/shared.ts:98), so there is no per-runtime advisor copy to collapse or drift.
